answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to complete a sequential verifiable-delay chain before it may transact: each step output seeds the next, so work cannot be parallelized across fake accounts. Like a vine that must grow one node at a time, an attacker spawning a thousand identities pays a thousand sequential waits, while honest agents pay once. Identities that misbehave are pruned and their chain voided, so the reef of trusted agents stays healthy instead of hollow: fake volume collapses because each fake costs real, unshareable time.
